references.text: God is not a man, so that he should lie. Should he say something and not do it? This underscores the theme in Genesis 41:32 that the matter has been firmly decided by God.
Isaiah 46:10-11 says that God declares the end from the beginning, and that his counsel will stand. He hastens to bring it to pass – directly parallel to God hurrying to do what he has decreed.
The word of the Lord tested Joseph until it came to pass, showing that God's word is firm and reliable, as Joseph explains in Genesis 41:32.
Isaiah 55:10-11 says that God's word does not return empty but accomplishes what he sends it to do – parallel to the matter being firmly decided by God and him hastening to bring it about.
2 Peter 3:9 says that the Lord is not slow in fulfilling his promise, relevant to the theme that God hurries to complete what he has determined.
The verses belong to the same event where a double dream confirms God's unchangeable decision.
Theological parallel: God's decisions are unshakable and will happen as he has determined.
